name: Mezzotint
summary: The plate is rocked with a toothed tool until it holds a full, velvet black; the engraver scrapes and burnishes the lights out of the dark. Ludwig von Siegen made the first in 1642; London engravers used it to reproduce portraits in oil.

philosophy.core_thesis: If the plate starts black, the artist works from dark to light and gets a tone as soft as paint, with no line.
design_principles: Start from a full black: rock the plate in 20–40 directions until every part holds ink.
Make each light by scraping and burnishing the grain flat; the more the scrape, the lighter the tone.
Model forms in soft, continuous tone; keep lines only for the finest details.
Set the subject against a deep, dark ground and bring the lights out of it.
Keep the darks velvet and slightly warm; avoid a pure white except at the highest lights.
anti_patterns: A hard outline round the forms
Visible hatching or a halftone dot
A white ground with dark forms on it

process.matrix: A copper plate, roughened all over with a curved, toothed rocker.
process.press: A roller press with felt blankets.
process.image_making: The engraver rocks the plate, then scrapes and burnishes the lights, and proofs it many times.
process.edition: Only 50–100 good impressions; the soft grain wears quickly, so early proofs are prized.

inks.strategy: One warm black or brown-black ink; a few prints use colour inks put on the plate by hand (à la poupée).

screening.rule: Make the tone with the rocked grain at about 100–150 dots a inch; the scrape sets the tone.

registration.rule: One plate prints all the image; there is no register.

substrate.stock: A soft laid or wove rag paper, dampened.

surface.impression: A plate mark and a soft, velvet ink film in the darks.
surface.sheen: Deep, matt black with a slight bloom.
surface.texture: A fine grain that the eye reads as continuous tone; under a lens it is a field of small pits.

marks: a worn grain in late impressions

emotion.target_response: Hush and depth: the viewer feels a candle-lit room and a face that comes out of the dark.

use_cases: editorial images on night or mystery
avoid_when: The image needs line or a bright, high-key mood.
The output prints on newsprint or on a coarse screen.

modifiers.how: Build the tone from swelling burin lines on a white plate.
Use a soft-focus platinum or gum print with the same deep tone.

sources.title: Carol Wax, The Mezzotint: History and Technique (Abrams, 1990)
